newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekistan to import 1.0-1.2 mln T food wheat.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan to import 1.0-1.2 mln T food wheat.

text.p: Uzbekistan will import 1.0-1.2 million tonnes of food wheat this year as its 1996 harvest of 2.7 million tonnes is not enough to cover domestic demand, an official Uzbek grain source said on Wednesday.
The source, speaking from the Uzbek capital Tashkent, added, "With the rise in food prices, the population in recent years has consumed more bread as the cheapest product."
The source said Uzbekistan would make grain purchases on European markets this month largely through U.S. grain trader Cargill and Swiss-owned Glencore.
He said grain might also be bought from the U.S. and Kazakhstan, but that less grain was likely to come from Russia.
Cargill's Tashkent office declined to comment.
Uzbek officials have said the former Soviet republic imported 1.6 million tonnes of grain in 1996.
The Central Asian state is aiming at self-sufficiency in grains, but is having problems attaining that goal.
"Uzbekistan will for the next few years make purchases on the world market as the quality of much of its own wheat does not meet food standards," the source said.
